problem: Cannot access a shared folder
description: The user tries to open a shared folder on another computer or server over the network, but the attempt fails generally, without a highly specific error, preventing any access to its contents.
symptoms: Double-clicking the shared folder does nothing or shows a generic error
A long delay occurs before any error appears
The folder was previously accessible but suddenly stopped working
Other network resources may still work normally
possible_causes: The host computer or server is turned off or disconnected from the network
File and printer sharing is disabled on the host computer
The user's account lacks permission to the specific share
A network connectivity problem between the user's computer and the host
The share itself was removed or renamed
diagnostic_questions: Is the computer or server hosting this folder turned on and connected to the network?
Have you accessed this shared folder successfully before?
Are other users able to access this same shared folder right now?
Do you know the exact network path, such as \\ServerName\FolderName?

commands.purpose: Check if the computer hosting the share is reachable on the network
commands.expected_result: Replies received from the host computer
commands.abnormal_result: Request timed out, meaning the host is off, disconnected, or unreachable

commands.purpose: List all shares available on the host computer
commands.expected_result: Shows a list of shared folder names on that computer
commands.abnormal_result: Error message, meaning the computer is unreachable or sharing is disabled there

troubleshooting_steps.action: Confirm the host computer or server is powered on and connected to the network
troubleshooting_steps.reason: A shared folder is only accessible while its host is running and reachable

troubleshooting_steps.action: Ping the host by name or IP to confirm basic network connectivity
troubleshooting_steps.reason: This verifies whether a network path currently exists before checking sharing-specific settings

troubleshooting_steps.action: Check with other users to see if they can access the same shared folder right now
troubleshooting_steps.reason: This determines if the problem is isolated to your account or computer, or affects the share more broadly

troubleshooting_steps.action: Confirm file and printer sharing is enabled on the host computer's network settings
troubleshooting_steps.reason: If sharing is disabled at the host, no other computer can reach any of its shared folders

troubleshooting_steps.action: Confirm your account has the correct permissions for this specific share, checking with the folder owner or administrator if uncertain
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Insufficient permissions will block access even when the host and network are otherwise healthy

troubleshooting_steps.action: Try accessing the share using its IP address instead of computer name
troubleshooting_steps.reason: This helps isolate whether the problem is with name resolution rather than the sharing itself

troubleshooting_steps.action: Restart the host computer if you have access to it, since this can clear temporary sharing service glitches
troubleshooting_steps.reason: A stuck or crashed sharing service on the host can prevent all access until restarted

possible_solutions: Restore power and network connectivity to the host computer
Enable file and printer sharing on the host
Request corrected permissions for the specific share
Access the share using its IP address if name resolution fails
Restart the host computer to clear a stuck sharing service
prevention: Keep host computers powered on and connected during business hours
Document and communicate share permissions clearly
Use a dedicated file server rather than individual desktops for critical shares
Periodically verify shared folder health

problem: Access denied when opening a shared folder
description: The user tries to open a shared folder and receives a specific 'Access is denied' message, indicating the connection to the host succeeded but permission to view the contents was refused.
symptoms: Error message specifically stating 'Access is denied'
The folder icon or path is visible but cannot be opened
Other shares on the same host may open normally
Problem may affect one user while others access it fine
possible_causes: The user's account is not listed in the folder's share or NTFS permissions
The user is logged in with a different account than the one granted access
The account's permission was recently changed or removed
A group membership change affected inherited permissions
Both share-level and file-level (NTFS) permissions exist, and one of them denies access
diagnostic_questions: Are you logged in with the account you believe should have access?
Have you accessed this folder successfully before with this same account?
Do other users with a similar role have successful access right now?
Do you know if your group membership or role changed recently?

commands.purpose: Confirm exactly which user account is currently logged in and attempting access
commands.expected_result: Shows the expected username that should have permission to the share
commands.abnormal_result: Shows an unexpected or different account than intended, explaining the denial

commands.purpose: Attempt a direct connection to the share and view the specific error returned
commands.expected_result: Command completes successfully
commands.abnormal_result: System error 5 (Access is denied) confirming a permissions problem rather than a connectivity one

troubleshooting_steps.action: Confirm you are logged in with the correct account that should have access to this share
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Being logged in with the wrong account is a very common and simple cause of an access denied error

troubleshooting_steps.action: Check both share-level permissions and NTFS (file-level) permissions on the folder, since both must allow access for the connection to succeed
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Windows applies the most restrictive of the two permission sets, so even correct share permissions can be blocked by restrictive NTFS permissions or vice versa

troubleshooting_steps.action: Confirm with the folder owner or administrator that your account or group is currently listed with appropriate permissions
troubleshooting_steps.reason: This directly verifies whether your access was ever granted, or was recently removed

troubleshooting_steps.action: If access depends on group membership, confirm your account is still a member of the expected group
troubleshooting_steps.reason: A recent change to group membership can silently remove previously working access

troubleshooting_steps.action: Request the folder owner or administrator add or restore the correct permissions for your account or group
troubleshooting_steps.reason: This directly resolves the root cause by granting the necessary access

troubleshooting_steps.action: After permissions are updated, log off and back on, or restart the computer, to ensure the new permissions are recognized
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Cached credentials and group membership tokens sometimes require a fresh login to reflect recent changes

possible_solutions: Log in with the correct account that has been granted access
Request the administrator correct share or NTFS permissions
Confirm and correct group membership affecting inherited access
Log off and back on after a permissions update to refresh credentials
prevention: Clearly document required permissions when a share is created
Communicate group membership changes that may affect access
Review share and NTFS permissions together when troubleshooting access

problem: Network path was not found
description: The user tries to access a shared folder by typing or clicking its network path, but Windows shows an error stating the network path was not found, indicating the target could not be located at all.
symptoms: Error message stating 'The network path was not found'
Typing the exact \\ComputerName\FolderName path fails
May happen with one specific share while others work
Often paired with Windows error code 0x80070035
possible_causes: The host computer name cannot be resolved to an IP address
The host computer is off, disconnected, or has changed its name or IP
The share was renamed, moved, or removed
A typo exists in the entered network path
A network routing or VLAN issue prevents reaching the host's subnet
diagnostic_questions: Is the exact spelling of the computer name and share name correct?
Has the host computer's name or IP address changed recently?
Are you on the same network or VLAN as the host computer?
Does this happen with just this one share, or all network paths?

commands.purpose: Check if the computer name can be resolved and reached
commands.expected_result: Replies received, confirming the name resolves and the host is reachable
commands.abnormal_result: 'Ping request could not find host', confirming a name resolution failure

commands.purpose: Directly check whether the computer name resolves to an IP address
commands.expected_result: Returns a valid IP address for the computer name
commands.abnormal_result: Non-existent domain or no answer, confirming the name cannot currently be resolved

troubleshooting_steps.action: Double-check the exact spelling of the network path being used, including the computer name and share name
troubleshooting_steps.reason: A simple typo is a common and easily overlooked cause of this exact error

troubleshooting_steps.action: Ping the host computer by name to check if it resolves and responds
troubleshooting_steps.reason: This confirms whether the problem is with locating the computer at all, versus a permissions issue after locating it

troubleshooting_steps.action: If the name does not resolve, try using the host's IP address directly instead of its name
troubleshooting_steps.reason: This helps confirm whether the issue is specifically with name resolution rather than the underlying connection

troubleshooting_steps.action: Confirm the host computer's name or IP address has not recently changed
troubleshooting_steps.reason: A renamed or re-addressed computer will break any previously saved paths or shortcuts pointing to its old name

troubleshooting_steps.action: Confirm your computer is on the same network or VLAN as the host, or that proper routing exists between them
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Computers on different, non-routed network segments cannot reach each other's shares even with correct names

troubleshooting_steps.action: Confirm with the folder owner or administrator that the share still exists under its expected name and has not been moved or removed
troubleshooting_steps.reason: A renamed, moved, or deleted share will always produce this exact error regardless of network health

troubleshooting_steps.action: If using a saved shortcut or mapped drive, delete and recreate it using the current, correct path
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Outdated saved paths will continue to fail even after the underlying issue, such as a renamed computer, is otherwise resolved

possible_solutions: Correct a typo in the network path
Use the host's IP address instead of its name
Update saved shortcuts or mapped drives with the current correct path
Resolve underlying VLAN or routing issues preventing reachability
Confirm the share still exists under its expected name with the administrator
prevention: Use consistent, documented naming for file servers and shares
Communicate server name or IP changes in advance
Avoid frequently renaming computers or shares that others depend on
Use DNS names rather than IP addresses where possible for easier management

problem: Shared folder is missing or cannot be found
description: The user goes to a location where a shared folder used to appear, such as a mapped drive or a bookmarked network location, but the folder itself is no longer listed or found there.
symptoms: The shared folder no longer appears in its expected location
Browsing the parent share shows fewer folders than expected
A previously working shortcut now leads to an error
Other shares on the same server remain visible and accessible
possible_causes: The specific folder was renamed by someone with appropriate permissions
The folder was moved to a different location on the server
The folder was deleted intentionally or accidentally
The user's permissions to view that specific folder were removed
A folder-level share was removed while the underlying folder still exists on disk
diagnostic_questions: When did you last successfully see and access this folder?
Do other users still see this folder in the same location?
Do you know of any recent reorganization of files on this server?
Are you looking in the exact same path as before, or could the location have changed?

troubleshooting_steps.action: Confirm you are browsing to the exact same path as before, since folders are sometimes reorganized into subfolders
troubleshooting_steps.reason: A folder may not be missing, but simply relocated within the same overall share structure

troubleshooting_steps.action: Check with other users who use the same shared folder to see if they still see it in its expected location
troubleshooting_steps.reason: This helps determine if the folder was genuinely removed for everyone, or if the issue is specific to your account's visibility or permissions

troubleshooting_steps.action: Ask colleagues or the folder owner if any recent reorganization, renaming, or cleanup effort took place on this server
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Planned changes are a common and straightforward explanation for a folder appearing to be missing

troubleshooting_steps.action: If your permissions to view this specific folder may have changed, confirm with the administrator whether your access was intentionally modified
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Some folder-level permission changes can make a folder invisible or inaccessible to specific users while it remains visible to others

troubleshooting_steps.action: If the folder was accidentally deleted, check with the server administrator about restoring it from a recent backup
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Accidental deletions are often recoverable from scheduled backups if reported and addressed promptly

troubleshooting_steps.action: Update any saved shortcuts or mapped drive references once the folder's current correct location is confirmed
troubleshooting_steps.reason: This ensures future access uses the correct, current path rather than an outdated one

troubleshooting_steps.action: Report the missing folder to the system or file server administrator with the exact expected path and when it was last seen
troubleshooting_steps.reason: This provides the specific detail needed to investigate whether it was moved, deleted, or a permissions issue

possible_solutions: Locate the folder in its new location if it was reorganized
Request restored permissions if visibility was intentionally or mistakenly changed
Restore the folder from a recent backup if it was accidentally deleted
Update saved shortcuts to reflect the folder's current correct path
prevention: Communicate planned reorganizations or renames to affected users in advance
Maintain regular backups of important shared folder structures
Document folder structure changes for reference

problem: Shared folder appears empty when it should contain files
description: The user successfully opens a shared folder, but it shows no files or subfolders, even though they and others expect specific content to be present.
symptoms: The folder opens without any error but shows zero items
Other users report seeing files that this user cannot see
The folder may show a correct file count in properties but display nothing
Problem may be limited to one folder or affect several
possible_causes: File-level permissions block visibility of individual files even though the folder itself is accessible
A filter or search term is still active in File Explorer, hiding non-matching files
The view has not refreshed and is showing a stale, empty cached state
Files were recently moved or deleted by another user
Hidden files setting is preventing certain items from displaying
diagnostic_questions: Do other users see files in this same folder right now?
Is there an active search or filter currently applied in File Explorer?
Have you tried refreshing the folder view or reopening the folder?
Could files have been recently moved or deleted by another user or process?

troubleshooting_steps.action: Clear any active search term or filter in the File Explorer address or search bar
troubleshooting_steps.reason: A leftover search term from previous browsing can cause the folder to display as empty if no files match it

troubleshooting_steps.action: Press F5 or otherwise refresh the folder view
troubleshooting_steps.reason: This clears a stale cached view and forces File Explorer to reload the folder's actual current contents

troubleshooting_steps.action: Check File Explorer's View settings to confirm hidden items are not the reason expected files are not showing
troubleshooting_steps.reason: If the expected files are intentionally hidden, they will not appear unless this setting is enabled

troubleshooting_steps.action: Check with other users to see if they can see files in this same folder right now
troubleshooting_steps.reason: This determines if the problem is specific to your visibility and permissions, or reflects the folder genuinely being empty for everyone

troubleshooting_steps.action: If other users see files but you do not, this suggests a file-level (NTFS) permission restriction specifically limiting your visibility
troubleshooting_steps.reason: It is possible to have access to a folder itself while being denied visibility of specific files or subfolders within it

troubleshooting_steps.action: Request the folder owner or administrator review and correct file-level permissions for your account if this is confirmed to be the cause
troubleshooting_steps.reason: This directly resolves a visibility restriction that is specific to certain files rather than the folder as a whole

troubleshooting_steps.action: If all users agree the folder is genuinely empty, investigate with the administrator whether files were recently moved, deleted, or affected by a backup or cleanup process
troubleshooting_steps.reason: This helps rule out or confirm actual data loss requiring recovery from backup

possible_solutions: Clear an active search or filter hiding the expected files
Refresh the folder view
Enable visibility of hidden files if applicable
Request corrected file-level permissions if visibility is restricted for your account
Investigate and restore from backup if files were genuinely removed
prevention: Clear filters and searches before assuming files are missing
Set consistent file-level permissions alongside folder-level permissions
Communicate before performing bulk file moves or deletions
keywords: folder empty but should have files

problem: Cannot browse the list of shared folders on a computer or server
description: The user tries to browse network locations to see a list of available shared folders on a specific computer or server, but the browsing itself fails, rather than being an issue with any one specific folder.
symptoms: Opening \\ComputerName in File Explorer fails to list any shares
Network browsing shows an empty result or an error
The user may still access a specific share directly by its full path even though browsing fails
Other computers may be browsable normally
possible_causes: Network discovery is turned off on the user's computer
The host computer has file and printer sharing disabled
A firewall is blocking the network browsing protocol
The host computer is not part of the same network segment or workgroup/domain
SMB browsing features have been deprecated or disabled on newer systems
diagnostic_questions: Can you access a specific known shared folder directly by typing its full path, even though browsing fails?
Is Network Discovery turned on in your Windows network settings?
Are you and the host computer on the same workgroup or domain?
Does browsing fail for all computers, or just this specific one?

commands.purpose: List computers visible on the network from the command line
commands.expected_result: Shows a list of computer names on the network
commands.abnormal_result: Error message or an empty list, suggesting a network browsing or discovery problem

troubleshooting_steps.action: Try accessing a specific known share directly by typing its full path, such as \\ComputerName\ShareName, rather than browsing
troubleshooting_steps.reason: This helps distinguish between a general network browsing failure and an actual connectivity or permissions problem with the specific share

troubleshooting_steps.action: Check that Network Discovery is turned on in your computer's Network and Sharing settings
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Network Discovery specifically controls the ability to see other computers when browsing the network, separate from actually connecting to a known share

troubleshooting_steps.action: Confirm the host computer also has Network Discovery and file/printer sharing enabled
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Both computers typically need these features enabled for browsing to work correctly between them

troubleshooting_steps.action: Confirm your computer and the host are on the same workgroup or domain, and ideally the same network segment
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Network browsing protocols often do not work well across different workgroups, domains, or routed network segments

troubleshooting_steps.action: Check if a firewall, either on your computer, the host, or a network device in between, might be blocking the specific ports used for network browsing
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Network browsing relies on specific protocols and ports that firewalls sometimes block even while direct share access still works

troubleshooting_steps.action: As a practical workaround, bookmark or save direct paths to frequently used shares rather than relying on browsing
troubleshooting_steps.reason: This avoids the need for browsing entirely for day-to-day access, since browsing itself is a convenience feature separate from the underlying share access

troubleshooting_steps.action: If browsing remains important and continues to fail, report the issue to the network administrator, since some organizations have deliberately disabled legacy browsing protocols for security reasons
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Modern security practices sometimes intentionally disable older network browsing features, which would explain a persistent, expected inability to browse

possible_solutions: Access known shares directly by their full path instead of browsing
Enable Network Discovery on both computers
Confirm both computers are on the same workgroup, domain, or network segment
Adjust firewall settings blocking network browsing protocols
Use saved direct paths as a practical workaround
prevention: Bookmark direct paths to frequently used shares
Keep Network Discovery settings consistent across company computers
Understand your organization's policy on legacy network browsing protocols

problem: Shared folder is unexpectedly read-only
description: The user can open a shared folder and view its files, but finds they cannot make any changes, save new files, or edit existing ones, with the folder behaving as if it is entirely read-only.
symptoms: Files can be opened and viewed, but not edited or saved
New files or folders cannot be created within the share
Editing tools may appear greyed out for files opened from this location
Other users may have full read-write access to the same folder
possible_causes: The user's account only has Read permission, not Write or Modify, for this share
The underlying NTFS permissions restrict write access even though share permissions allow it
The folder or specific files have the read-only attribute set
The share was intentionally configured as read-only for general users
A group membership change reduced the user's access level
diagnostic_questions: Do other users have full read-write access to this same shared folder?
Have you had write access to this folder before, or is this your first time needing to save something here?
Do you know if this share is intentionally meant to be read-only for general users?
Are you trying to edit an existing file, or create a brand new one?

troubleshooting_steps.action: Check with other users to confirm whether they have full read-write access to this same shared folder
troubleshooting_steps.reason: This helps determine if the read-only behavior is specific to your account, or intentional for all general users of this share

troubleshooting_steps.action: Consider whether this share was ever intended to be read-only for your role, such as a folder meant only for viewing reference documents
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Some shares are deliberately configured as read-only by business design, which would mean this behavior is expected rather than a technical fault

troubleshooting_steps.action: If write access is genuinely needed and was expected, confirm with the folder owner or administrator what your current share and NTFS permission levels are
troubleshooting_steps.reason: This clarifies your exact current access level and confirms whether it needs to be upgraded

troubleshooting_steps.action: Request the folder owner or administrator grant Write or Modify permission at both the share and NTFS level if write access is needed and currently missing
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Both permission layers need to allow write access for the user to actually be able to save or edit files

troubleshooting_steps.action: If a specific individual file (rather than the whole folder) appears read-only, check that file's own Properties for a locally set read-only attribute
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Individual files can have their own read-only attribute set independently of the folder's general permissions

troubleshooting_steps.action: After permissions are updated, log off and back on, or restart the computer, to ensure the new access level is properly recognized
troubleshooting_steps.reason: This ensures the updated permissions take full effect in your current session

possible_solutions: Confirm whether read-only access is intentional for this share
Request an upgrade to Write or Modify permission from the administrator
Remove a read-only attribute from a specific file if applicable
Log off and back on after a permission change to apply it
prevention: Clearly document the intended access level for each share
Communicate permission level changes to affected users
Confirm expected access level when first granted a new share

problem: Cannot map a network drive
description: The user tries to set up a mapped network drive pointing to a shared folder, assigning it a drive letter for easy access, but the mapping process fails with an error.
symptoms: Error message when attempting to map the network drive
The mapping process appears to complete but the drive does not appear in File Explorer
Error mentions the network path, permissions, or an already-used drive letter
Previously successful mapping now fails
possible_causes: The network path entered is incorrect or has a typo
The chosen drive letter is already in use by another mapped drive or device
The user's account lacks permission to the target share
The host computer or server is currently unreachable
Saved credentials for the share are outdated or incorrect
diagnostic_questions: What is the exact network path and drive letter you are trying to use?
Have you successfully mapped this same drive before?
Is the drive letter you are choosing already used by something else, such as a USB drive?
Are you being prompted for credentials, and if so, are you confident they are correct?

commands.purpose: Attempt to map the network drive from the command line and view any specific error returned
commands.expected_result: Command completes successfully, confirming the drive was mapped
commands.abnormal_result: A specific system error number is returned, such as error 53 or 67, pointing to the exact underlying cause

troubleshooting_steps.action: Double-check the exact network path being entered for typos, including the computer name and share name
troubleshooting_steps.reason: A simple typo in the path is one of the most common reasons a drive mapping attempt fails

troubleshooting_steps.action: Try mapping to a different, unused drive letter
troubleshooting_steps.reason: The originally chosen letter may already be assigned to another device or mapped drive, which would block the mapping

troubleshooting_steps.action: Confirm the host server is currently reachable by pinging it or testing another known share on the same server
troubleshooting_steps.reason: The mapping attempt cannot succeed if the underlying server or share itself is currently unreachable

troubleshooting_steps.action: If prompted for credentials, confirm you are entering the correct username and password, including the correct domain prefix if required
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Incorrect or improperly formatted credentials are a common cause of a failed mapping attempt, especially on domain networks

troubleshooting_steps.action: Clear any previously saved, outdated credentials for this server using Windows Credential Manager before trying again
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Old, cached credentials can interfere with a new mapping attempt even when the currently entered credentials are correct

troubleshooting_steps.action: Confirm your account has the necessary permissions to access the target share, checking with the administrator if uncertain
troubleshooting_steps.reason: A mapping attempt will fail if the underlying account does not have permission to the share it is trying to connect to

troubleshooting_steps.action: Try mapping the drive using the net use command from Command Prompt to see the exact system error number returned, which provides more specific diagnostic detail
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Command-line mapping attempts often return more precise error codes than the graphical interface, helping pinpoint the exact cause

possible_solutions: Correct a typo in the network path
Choose a different, unused drive letter
Enter correct credentials, including any required domain prefix
Clear outdated saved credentials in Credential Manager
Request corrected share permissions from the administrator
prevention: Save correct network paths for reference to avoid future typos
Use a consistent drive letter convention across mapped drives
Keep saved credentials up to date after any password change

problem: Network drive shows as disconnected or fails to reconnect
description: A previously mapped network drive now shows a disconnected status, often indicated by a red X on the drive icon, and attempts to automatically or manually reconnect it fail.
symptoms: Drive icon in File Explorer shows a red X
Clicking the drive prompts a reconnection attempt that fails
Drive worked normally in a previous session but is disconnected now
Error appears when Windows tries to reconnect the drive at startup
possible_causes: The host server was unreachable at the time Windows tried to reconnect, such as during startup
Saved credentials for the drive have become invalid, often after a password change
The host server or share is temporarily unavailable
A network connectivity problem at the time of the reconnection attempt
The share itself was removed, renamed, or permissions changed
diagnostic_questions: Does the drive reconnect successfully if you double-click it manually?
Was your account password changed recently?
Is the host server currently reachable and are other people able to access this share?
Does this happen every time you start the computer, or only occasionally?

commands.purpose: Confirm the host server is currently reachable
commands.expected_result: Replies received from the server
commands.abnormal_result: Request timed out, meaning the server is currently unreachable, explaining the failed reconnection

commands.purpose: View the current status of all mapped drives and any associated error information
commands.expected_result: Shows the drive as OK and connected
commands.abnormal_result: Shows the drive status as 'Disconnected' or 'Unavailable', confirming the reconnection failure

troubleshooting_steps.action: Double-click the disconnected drive icon to attempt a manual reconnection
troubleshooting_steps.reason: This is the simplest first step and often succeeds even when an automatic reconnection at startup failed

troubleshooting_steps.action: If prompted for credentials during the manual reconnection, enter the current, correct username and password
troubleshooting_steps.reason: A recent password change is a very common reason saved credentials used for automatic reconnection become invalid

troubleshooting_steps.action: Confirm the host server is currently reachable by pinging it or checking if others can access the same share
troubleshooting_steps.reason: If the server itself is down or unreachable, no reconnection attempt, automatic or manual, will succeed until it comes back online

troubleshooting_steps.action: If the drive disconnects specifically and consistently right after computer startup, this may indicate the network connection is not yet fully established when Windows attempts the automatic reconnection
troubleshooting_steps.reason: On some systems, especially with VPN connections, the network may not be ready quickly enough for automatic drive reconnection to succeed at login

troubleshooting_steps.action: Update saved credentials for this drive in Windows Credential Manager if a password change is the confirmed cause
troubleshooting_steps.reason: This ensures future automatic reconnection attempts use the current, correct password

troubleshooting_steps.action: If disconnections are frequent and related to network timing at startup, consider removing and recreating the mapped drive with the persistent connection option properly enabled
troubleshooting_steps.reason: This can sometimes resolve stubborn reconnection issues by refreshing the drive's underlying configuration

troubleshooting_steps.action: If the problem continues despite correct credentials and a reachable server, report it to the network administrator, since it may indicate an intermittent server-side or network issue
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Persistent, unexplained reconnection failures may point to a deeper infrastructure issue requiring administrator investigation

possible_solutions: Manually reconnect the drive with current credentials
Update outdated saved credentials in Credential Manager
Wait for the host server to become reachable again
Remove and recreate the mapped drive if reconnection issues persist
Report persistent unexplained failures to the network administrator
prevention: Update saved credentials promptly after any password change
Ensure VPN or network connections are established before relying on automatic drive reconnection
Use persistent connection settings when originally mapping the drive

problem: Mapped network drive is missing after restarting the computer
description: A network drive that was previously mapped and set to reconnect automatically no longer appears at all in File Explorer after the computer is restarted, rather than showing as disconnected.
symptoms: The mapped drive letter does not appear at all in File Explorer
The drive was working normally before the restart
Manually remapping the drive works temporarily until the next restart
No error message appears since the drive is simply absent
possible_causes: The drive was not originally mapped with the 'reconnect at sign-in' option enabled
A Group Policy setting is intentionally preventing persistent drive mappings
The mapping was removed by a login script or management tool
User profile or registry corruption affecting saved drive mapping information
The drive was mapped under a different user account than the one currently logged in
diagnostic_questions: When you originally mapped this drive, did you select the option to reconnect at sign-in?
Is this a personal or a company-managed computer with possible policy restrictions?
Does the drive come back if you manually remap it, only to disappear again after the next restart?
Are you logging in with the same user account each time?

commands.purpose: Check the current status of any mapped drives associated with this session
commands.expected_result: Shows the drive as mapped and connected
commands.abnormal_result: The drive does not appear in the list at all, confirming it was not persisted through the restart

troubleshooting_steps.action: Remap the drive and specifically ensure the 'Reconnect at sign-in' (or 'Reconnect at logon') checkbox is selected during the mapping process
troubleshooting_steps.reason: If this option was not selected originally, the drive mapping is only temporary for that single session and will not persist through a restart

troubleshooting_steps.action: Confirm you are logging in with the same user account each time, since drive mappings are typically tied to a specific user profile

troubleshooting_steps.action: On a company-managed computer, check with the IT department whether a Group Policy or login script is intentionally managing drive mappings

possible_solutions: Use the server's IP address as an immediate workaround
Flush the local DNS cache
Connect to the correct internal network or VPN for internal DNS resolution
Have the administrator correct an outdated DNS record after a server IP change
prevention: Update DNS records promptly whenever a server's IP address changes
Ensure remote users have proper VPN access to internal DNS when needed
Periodically verify critical server DNS records remain accurate

problem: Firewall is blocking file sharing access
description: The user has a working network connection to the general area of the file server, but a firewall, either on their own computer, the server, or a network device in between, is specifically blocking the ports needed for file sharing to function.
symptoms: The server responds to a basic ping, but shares still cannot be accessed
Error messages specifically related to connection refusal rather than the server being unreachable
Problem may have started after installing new antivirus or security software
Access works fine on some networks but not others, such as a new office location
possible_causes: Windows Firewall on the user's computer is blocking outgoing file sharing connections
Windows Firewall on the file server is blocking incoming file sharing connections
A network firewall or security appliance between the two networks is blocking the specific SMB ports
Newly installed antivirus or security software introduced its own firewall blocking file sharing
A recent security policy update tightened firewall rules affecting file sharing
diagnostic_questions: Does the server respond to a basic ping, even though the actual share connection fails?
Did this start right after installing new antivirus or security software?
Does this happen on all networks, or specifically one location, such as a new office or remote connection?
Are other users on the same network experiencing the same specific issue?

commands.purpose: Test if the SMB file sharing port (445) is open and reachable on the file server

commands.abnormal_result: 'Could not open connection', confirming the specific SMB port is being blocked somewhere along the path

troubleshooting_steps.action: Confirm the server responds to a basic ping, which helps establish that general network connectivity exists, even if the specific file sharing ports are blocked
troubleshooting_steps.reason: This narrows the problem down specifically to file sharing ports being blocked, rather than a complete network unreachability issue

troubleshooting_steps.action: Test whether the specific SMB port (typically port 445) is reachable using a tool like telnet
troubleshooting_steps.reason: This directly tests whether the specific port required for file sharing is open, isolating the problem to that exact port rather than general connectivity

troubleshooting_steps.action: Temporarily disable Windows Firewall on your own computer to test if it is the source of the block, remembering to turn it back on afterward
troubleshooting_steps.reason: This quickly confirms whether your own computer's firewall is the cause, versus something on the server or network side

troubleshooting_steps.action: If disabling your firewall resolves the issue, add an appropriate exception for file and printer sharing in Windows Firewall rather than leaving it permanently disabled
troubleshooting_steps.reason: This maintains your computer's security while specifically allowing the necessary file sharing traffic

troubleshooting_steps.action: If a newly installed antivirus or security program is suspected, check its separate firewall settings for file sharing exceptions
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Many antivirus programs include their own independent firewall that can block traffic even when Windows Firewall itself is properly configured

troubleshooting_steps.action: If your own computer's firewall settings appear correct, check with the network or server administrator whether the file server's firewall allows incoming connections from your specific network location
troubleshooting_steps.reason: The block could be on the receiving end rather than your own computer, especially if this is a new office or network location

troubleshooting_steps.action: If a network firewall or security appliance sits between your location and the server, such as when connecting from a different office, ask the network administrator to confirm the necessary file sharing ports are allowed between these specific network segments
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Inter-office or inter-segment firewalls are a common but often overlooked source of blocked file sharing traffic in larger organizations

possible_solutions: Add a file and printer sharing exception in Windows Firewall
Adjust third-party antivirus firewall settings to allow file sharing
Have the administrator open the necessary port on the file server's firewall
Request the network administrator allow file sharing traffic between specific network segments
prevention: Document required firewall exceptions for file sharing across the organization
Test file sharing access after installing new security software
Coordinate firewall rule changes with IT before connecting from new network locations

problem: VPN is not connected, preventing access to shared folders

VPN client shows as disconnected or not running
Access works fine when physically in the office, but not remotely
possible_causes: The VPN client was not started or connected before attempting to access internal resources
The VPN connection dropped unexpectedly at some point during the work session
Incorrect VPN credentials or an expired VPN certificate is preventing connection
A local internet connectivity issue is preventing the VPN itself from establishing
diagnostic_questions: Is your VPN client currently showing as connected or disconnected?
Are you able to access general internet websites normally at the moment?
Have you successfully connected to this VPN and accessed shares before?
Did the VPN connection possibly drop partway through your work session?

troubleshooting_steps.action: Check your VPN client's current status to confirm whether it shows as connected or disconnected
troubleshooting_steps.reason: This is the most direct and immediate check, since internal shares are typically completely unreachable without an active VPN connection

troubleshooting_steps.action: If disconnected, start and connect the VPN client using your normal credentials
troubleshooting_steps.reason: This directly establishes the required connection to the internal company network needed to reach shared folders

troubleshooting_steps.action: Confirm your general internet connection is working normally, since a working internet connection is required before the VPN itself can even attempt to connect
troubleshooting_steps.reason: A VPN cannot establish a connection without a working underlying internet connection to build upon

troubleshooting_steps.action: Once the VPN shows as successfully connected, try accessing the shared folder again
troubleshooting_steps.reason: This confirms whether the VPN connection alone was the missing piece needed to restore access

troubleshooting_steps.action: If the VPN fails to connect with an error, such as an authentication failure, follow standard VPN troubleshooting, including double-checking your credentials
troubleshooting_steps.reason: A failed VPN connection attempt itself needs to be resolved before shared folder access, which depends on it, can be expected to work

troubleshooting_steps.action: If the VPN was connected but access still fails, or the VPN disconnects shortly after connecting, check for a stable, strong internet connection, since an unstable connection can cause VPN drops
troubleshooting_steps.reason: An intermittently dropping VPN connection would explain access that seems to work briefly before failing again

troubleshooting_steps.action: Contact IT support if the VPN consistently fails to connect or maintain a stable connection despite correct credentials and a working internet connection
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Persistent VPN connectivity issues may require administrator-level investigation into the VPN server or your specific account configuration

possible_solutions: Start and connect the VPN client before accessing internal shares
Confirm and restore general internet connectivity first if needed
Resolve VPN authentication issues if the connection attempt itself fails
Contact IT support for persistent VPN connectivity problems
prevention: Always connect the VPN before attempting to access internal resources remotely
Keep VPN client software updated
Maintain a stable, reliable internet connection when working remotely

A conflict with security software interfering with the SMB service
SMB has been intentionally disabled as part of a security hardening configuration
diagnostic_questions: Does this affect all file sharing from this specific computer, or just one particular share?

commands.purpose: Check the status of the 'Server' service, which is responsible for SMB file sharing, on the host computer

commands.abnormal_result: The service is stopped, confirming it as the direct cause of the complete file sharing failure

troubleshooting_steps.action: On the host computer, open the Services management console and check the status of the 'Server' service

troubleshooting_steps.action: If the Server service is stopped, start it manually and set its startup type to Automatic if it is not already configured that way
troubleshooting_steps.reason: This directly restores file sharing functionality and helps ensure it starts properly on future restarts

troubleshooting_steps.action: Restart the host computer, since this often resolves an underlying issue that caused the service to stop in the first place
troubleshooting_steps.reason: A fresh restart clears many temporary conditions that can cause core Windows services to become unresponsive

troubleshooting_steps.action: Check for and install any pending Windows updates on the host computer, since some update-related issues affecting SMB have been resolved in subsequent updates
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Keeping the system current addresses known bugs that may be specifically affecting the SMB service

troubleshooting_steps.action: Check third-party security software installed on the host computer for any settings that might be interfering with or blocking the SMB service
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Some security software can interfere with core Windows services, including those responsible for file sharing

troubleshooting_steps.action: Confirm whether SMB has been intentionally disabled as part of a security policy, especially if this is a recently hardened or newly configured computer
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Some organizations intentionally disable or restrict SMB for security reasons, which would mean this behavior is expected rather than a malfunction

troubleshooting_steps.action: If the Server service repeatedly stops on its own after being restarted, check the Windows Event Viewer for specific error details, and escalate to IT support for deeper investigation
troubleshooting_steps.reason: A service that repeatedly crashes indicates an underlying problem that requires more detailed log analysis to properly diagnose and fix

possible_solutions: Start the Server service and set it to Automatic startup
Restart the host computer
Install pending Windows updates that may address known SMB issues
Adjust third-party security software interfering with the service
Escalate a repeatedly crashing service to IT for deeper investigation
prevention: Keep the host computer's Windows updates current
Set the Server service to Automatic startup
Monitor for repeated service crashes as an early warning sign of a deeper issue

problem: SMB version mismatch preventing connection
description: The user's computer and the file server use different, incompatible versions of the SMB file sharing protocol, causing the connection to fail even though both systems are otherwise online and reachable.
symptoms: Connection specifically fails with an error referencing protocol or version compatibility
Older devices cannot connect to newer, more securely configured servers, or vice versa
The server and client both respond to basic network tests, but sharing specifically fails
Problem is more common when connecting older equipment to modern, hardened servers
possible_causes: The server has disabled older, insecure SMB versions (such as SMBv1) that an older client still relies on
The client computer has disabled a newer SMB version that the server requires
A significant version gap exists between very old and very new systems with no overlapping compatible version
Security hardening on one side removed support for a protocol version still needed by the other side
diagnostic_questions: Is this an older computer or device trying to connect to a newer, more recently configured server, or the reverse?
Do other, more modern computers connect to this same server successfully?
Do you know if SMBv1 has been intentionally disabled anywhere in this environment for security reasons?
What operating system versions are involved on both the client and server side?

commands.purpose: Check which SMB protocol versions are currently enabled on a Windows computer acting as the server (run in PowerShell)
commands.expected_result: Shows the currently enabled SMB protocol versions
commands.abnormal_result: Shows that the specific version needed by the client, or by the server for the client, is disabled

troubleshooting_steps.action: Confirm whether the issue involves an older device connecting to a newer server, or the reverse, and note the specific operating systems involved
troubleshooting_steps.reason: This helps identify which side is likely missing support for a version the other side requires

troubleshooting_steps.action: Check with other, more modern computers to see if they can connect to the same server successfully
troubleshooting_steps.reason: This helps confirm whether the issue is specific to the older or differently configured client, rather than a broader server problem

troubleshooting_steps.action: Recognize that older, insecure SMB versions like SMBv1 are increasingly disabled by default on modern systems for important security reasons
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Understanding this context helps frame the appropriate solution as updating the outdated component rather than simply re-enabling an insecure legacy protocol

troubleshooting_steps.action: Where possible, prioritize updating or replacing the outdated device or operating system to support modern, secure SMB versions
troubleshooting_steps.reason: This addresses the root cause properly by bringing the outdated component up to current security standards, rather than weakening the more modern, secure system

troubleshooting_steps.action: If updating the outdated device is not immediately possible, and after careful security consideration, an administrator may need to temporarily enable an older SMB version specifically for that legacy connection
troubleshooting_steps.reason: This is a security trade-off that should only be made deliberately, ideally paired with a plan to fully phase out the legacy dependency as soon as possible

troubleshooting_steps.action: Use the Get-SmbServerConfiguration PowerShell command on the relevant Windows computer to check exactly which SMB versions are currently enabled
troubleshooting_steps.reason: This provides precise technical confirmation of the current configuration, useful for the administrator making any necessary adjustment

troubleshooting_steps.action: Document any legacy SMB version support that is enabled as a temporary exception, along with a plan and timeline to eventually remove the outdated dependency
troubleshooting_steps.reason: This ensures the security trade-off remains temporary and intentional, rather than becoming an unmanaged, permanent weakness

possible_solutions: Update or replace the outdated device or operating system to support modern SMB versions
Have an administrator deliberately and temporarily enable an older SMB version if truly necessary
Document and plan to phase out any legacy SMB version dependency
Confirm exact current SMB configuration using PowerShell commands
prevention: Keep all devices updated to support modern, secure SMB versions
Plan proactively to retire legacy equipment relying on outdated protocols
Avoid re-enabling insecure legacy protocols except as a carefully managed, temporary exception

problem: File sharing or Network Discovery is disabled
description: The computer's overall settings have file sharing or network discovery turned off, preventing it from either sharing its own folders with others, seeing other computers on the network, or both.
symptoms: The computer cannot see other computers when browsing the network
Other computers cannot see or access shares hosted on this computer
Network and Sharing Center shows sharing options as turned off
Problem affects this specific computer while others on the same network work normally
possible_causes: File sharing and Network Discovery were never enabled on this computer
These settings were turned off intentionally or accidentally at some point
The network location profile is set to 'Public' rather than 'Private', which uses more restrictive default settings
A security policy specifically disabled these features on this computer
diagnostic_questions: Is this happening on your own computer (unable to share out), another computer you are trying to reach, or both?
Do you know what network profile, such as Private or Public, this computer is currently using?
Has file sharing worked on this specific computer before?
Is this a personal computer or a company-managed one with possible policy restrictions?

troubleshooting_steps.action: Open Network and Sharing Center (or the equivalent Network settings) and check the current status of Network Discovery and File and Printer Sharing
troubleshooting_steps.reason: This directly shows whether these essential features are currently turned on or off

troubleshooting_steps.action: If disabled, turn on both Network Discovery and File and Printer Sharing
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Both of these features generally need to be enabled for a computer to properly participate in file sharing on the network, either as a host or a client browsing for others

troubleshooting_steps.action: Check the current network profile assigned to your active connection, confirming whether it is set to Private or Public

troubleshooting_steps.action: If you are on a trusted network, such as your home or office, and it is incorrectly marked as Public, change the network profile to Private
troubleshooting_steps.reason: This applies the more permissive default settings appropriate for a trusted network, which typically includes enabling file sharing features more readily

troubleshooting_steps.action: On a company-managed computer, check with IT whether these settings are being centrally controlled by a security policy
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Organizations sometimes intentionally restrict these features by policy, meaning a manual change might be reverted, or might not be the appropriate expected solution

troubleshooting_steps.action: After making changes, restart the computer or at least the relevant network services to ensure the new settings are fully applied

troubleshooting_steps.action: Test both browsing to other computers and confirming other computers can now see and access shares on this one
troubleshooting_steps.reason: This confirms both directions of the desired functionality are now working properly

possible_solutions: Enable Network Discovery and File and Printer Sharing
Change the network profile from Public to Private for trusted networks
Confirm and align with any company IT policy governing these settings
Restart the computer or relevant services after making changes
prevention: Confirm correct network profile assignment when connecting to new trusted networks
Document expected sharing settings for company computers
Understand your organization's policy on network discovery and sharing defaults

problem: File upload or download fails on a shared or web-connected folder

Problem may happen with all files, or specifically large ones
possible_causes: A network interruption occurred during the transfer
The file exceeds a size limit imposed by the destination or transfer method
Insufficient permissions at the source or destination for the specific transfer direction
Insufficient storage space at the destination
A temporary server-side issue affecting file transfer capability
diagnostic_questions: Does this happen with all files, or specifically large ones?
Is your network connection stable throughout the attempted transfer?
Have you successfully uploaded or downloaded files to this same location before?
Does the error give any specific reason, such as a size limit or permissions issue?

troubleshooting_steps.action: Check your network connection stability, since an interrupted connection during a transfer is one of the most common causes of upload or download failures
troubleshooting_steps.reason: A dropped connection partway through directly causes an incomplete or failed transfer

troubleshooting_steps.action: If the file is unusually large, check if there is a known size limit for this specific upload or download method
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Many systems impose maximum file size limits, and exceeding this will cause the transfer to fail, sometimes without a very clear error

troubleshooting_steps.action: If the file is large, try compressing it or splitting it into smaller parts if the destination and use case allow this approach
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Reducing the file size can bring it within allowed limits and also reduces the chance of a network interruption affecting the transfer

troubleshooting_steps.action: Confirm you have the correct permissions for the specific direction of transfer, such as read access for downloading from the source, or write access for uploading to the destination

troubleshooting_steps.action: Check available storage space at the destination, since insufficient space will prevent an upload from completing successfully

troubleshooting_steps.action: Retry the transfer after a brief pause, in case this was a temporary, one-time network or server issue
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Some transfer failures are caused by brief, non-repeating glitches that succeed on a subsequent attempt

troubleshooting_steps.action: If transfers of this type consistently fail despite these checks, report the issue to the system or network administrator with specific details about file size and the exact error encountered
troubleshooting_steps.reason: This provides the necessary information to investigate a potential systemic limit or server-side issue affecting file transfers

possible_solutions: Ensure a stable network connection throughout the transfer
Reduce file size through compression or splitting if size limits are the issue
Confirm correct permissions for the specific transfer direction
Free up storage space at the destination
Report persistent transfer failures to the administrator with specific details
prevention: Maintain a stable network connection for important file transfers
Be aware of file size limits before attempting large transfers
Monitor destination storage space regularly
Compress large files proactively when appropriate

problem: File copy or move operation fails or is interrupted

Insufficient permissions for specific files within a larger folder structure
The destination has run out of available storage space partway through
A very long file path or file name exceeding system limits for certain files
diagnostic_questions: Does the failure happen with all files being copied or moved, or just some specific ones?
Is your network connection stable throughout the operation?
Do you know if any of the files involved might currently be open or in use?
How large is the overall amount of data being copied or moved?

troubleshooting_steps.action: Note whether the failure affects the entire operation, or just specific individual files within a larger batch

troubleshooting_steps.action: Check your network connection stability throughout the operation, especially for very large transfers
troubleshooting_steps.reason: A network interruption partway through a large copy or move operation is a very common cause of failure

troubleshooting_steps.action: If specific files consistently fail, check whether they might currently be open or locked by another user or process

troubleshooting_steps.action: Check available storage space at the destination, especially for very large copy operations

troubleshooting_steps.action: For specific files that consistently fail, check if their full file path, including all folder names, might be unusually long, potentially exceeding system path length limits

troubleshooting_steps.action: For very large batches, consider breaking the operation into smaller batches rather than attempting to copy or move everything at once

troubleshooting_steps.action: If certain files consistently and specifically fail despite these checks, report them to the system administrator, since they may require special handling or indicate an underlying corruption or permissions issue
troubleshooting_steps.reason: Consistently failing specific files often point to a distinct, isolated issue with those particular items rather than a general operational problem

possible_solutions: Ensure a stable network connection for large operations
Close files that are locked or in use before retrying
Free up destination storage space before large copy operations
Break very large batches into smaller, more manageable operations
Report consistently failing specific files to the administrator
prevention: Maintain a stable network connection for large file operations
Avoid excessively long, deeply nested folder and file naming structures

Close files properly before they need to be copied or moved by others

troubleshooting_steps.reason: This distinguishes between an individual quota limit and an overall storage capacity issue, which require different approaches to resolve

troubleshooting_steps.action: Check with other users to see if they are also experiencing storage-related errors on this same shared location
troubleshooting_steps.reason: This helps determine if the issue is your individual quota specifically, or a broader problem with the overall available storage

troubleshooting_steps.action: Review your own files within this location for anything old, unnecessary, or duplicated that could be deleted or archived to free up space

troubleshooting_steps.action: Delete or move unnecessary files to a different, more appropriate location, such as a personal archive or a location with less strict quota limits

troubleshooting_steps.action: If you believe your current quota is genuinely insufficient for legitimate business needs, contact the system administrator to discuss a possible quota increase

troubleshooting_steps.action: As a proactive habit, periodically review and clean up unnecessary files in frequently used shared locations
troubleshooting_steps.reason: This helps prevent storage issues from recurring and keeps shared locations more organized overall

possible_solutions: Delete or archive unnecessary personal files to free up quota space
Move files to a different location with more available space
Request a quota increase from the administrator if genuinely needed
Report an overall server capacity issue to the administrator
prevention: Periodically review and clean up unnecessary files
Understand your assigned storage quota and monitor usage against it
Request appropriate quota levels proactively for known large storage needs
Archive completed or older project files to reduce active storage usage

problem: Shared folder opens slowly or File Explorer freezes while browsing it

The file server itself is under heavy load, slowing down its response to browsing requests

Does this happen with all folders on this share, or specifically this one large folder?
Are other users experiencing similar slowness opening this same folder?

troubleshooting_steps.action: Check approximately how many files and subfolders exist within this specific folder

troubleshooting_steps.action: Switch the folder's view to a simpler list view rather than large icons or thumbnails, if not already using one

troubleshooting_steps.action: Check with other users to see if they experience similar slowness opening this same specific folder
troubleshooting_steps.reason: This helps determine if the issue is specific to your computer and connection, or reflects a genuine characteristic of this particular folder or the server's current load

troubleshooting_steps.action: Check your own network connection stability and speed, since a slow connection will make browsing any large folder feel more sluggish
troubleshooting_steps.reason: General network performance directly affects how quickly a large folder listing can be transferred and displayed

troubleshooting_steps.action: If antivirus software is configured to scan network locations in real time, check if this might be contributing to the delay when browsing this particular folder

troubleshooting_steps.action: If this specific folder has grown to contain an excessive number of files over time, consider working with the folder owner to reorganize its contents into logical subfolders

troubleshooting_steps.action: If the slowness seems related to overall server performance rather than this specific folder's size, report the pattern to the system administrator
troubleshooting_steps.reason: This helps distinguish a folder-specific organizational issue from a broader server performance problem that needs administrator attention

possible_solutions: Switch to a simple list view instead of thumbnails
Reorganize an excessively large folder into logical subfolders
Adjust antivirus real-time scanning settings for network locations if contributing to delays
Report broader server performance issues to the administrator
prevention: Proactively organize large folders into logical subfolders as they grow
Use list view rather than thumbnail view for folders with many files
Periodically review and archive old files from frequently browsed large folders

problem: Offline files are not synchronizing correctly

Files on the server are not reflected in the local offline cache

problem: VLAN or network configuration issue prevents reaching the file server
description: In a business network using VLANs (Virtual Local Area Networks) to segment traffic, a user on one VLAN is unable to reach a file server located on a different VLAN, due to a routing or configuration issue between the segments.
symptoms: The file server is completely unreachable, including failing a basic ping, specifically from certain locations or network segments
Users on the same VLAN as the server access it normally
The problem is consistent from specific physical locations or specific network jacks/Wi-Fi zones
Other resources on the user's own local VLAN work normally
possible_causes: Inter-VLAN routing between the user's VLAN and the server's VLAN is missing or misconfigured
A firewall or access control list between VLANs is blocking the necessary traffic
The user's device is on an unexpected or incorrect VLAN due to a switch port or Wi-Fi configuration issue
A recent network change altered VLAN routing without accounting for this specific access need
diagnostic_questions: Can you reach other resources on your own local network normally, with only this specific server being unreachable?
Do users in other locations or on other network segments access this same server without any problem?
Has your physical location, network jack, or Wi-Fi access point changed recently?
Has there been any recent network infrastructure change, such as new switches or a network redesign?
